identity.description:
Close an orchestrator item in one pass, unlock dead locks and delete each proven branch

## Summary

The close of an orchestrator item now needs one pass and leaves nothing behind. `stop` waits after it closes the tab until the session process has ended, and `remove` waits a short time for a session that is still ending, so the orchestrator does not have to run `remove` a second time. `remove` now removes a worktree whose git lock names a process that no longer runs, and still refuses a lock whose owner runs or cannot be proven dead. With `--delete-branch`, `remove` now deletes every local branch of the item (the launcher's `worktree-<name>` branch, the branch the project lead moved the worktree to, and the deliverable and package branches of the project lead's goal record), but only a branch whose every commit is on a branch or tag that origin lists now, or on the merged PR's head. Each other branch stays, and the close puts one notice in the inbox that names it.

Closes #167

**Ticket:** [#167 — Orchestrator close-out: one pass, dead locks, and no merged branch left behind](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/issues/167)
**Type:** Bug fix

---

## Agent context

### Authority

- `docs/design.md` §15.145 (why `remove` forces nothing) and the new §15.147 (each choice of this change, with its reason).
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md` owns `stop` and `remove`: the waits, the lock rule, the branch candidates, the proof and the output.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/resume-and-close.md` owns the close of an item: which flags step 3 gives, and the one inbox notice.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/launcher.py`: `stop` waits up to 15 seconds after the close for each `claude` pid that was still on the tty, and sends no signal. `remove` waits up to 15 seconds when each blocker is a `claude` with no terminal. `remove` reads the worktree lock after that wait: it unlocks only a lock whose reason names exactly one pid that is not running, tests that pid again right before `git worktree unlock`, and refuses every other lock with exit 9. `--delete-branch` takes candidates from the checked-out branch, `worktree-<name>` and the goal records whose `run.repo` is the worktree and whose `run.created_at` is not before the worktree was made (review records excluded). It never takes the default branch. It proves each candidate with `git rev-list refs/heads/<c> --stdin` against keepers that are only the shas that `git ls-remote origin` lists under `refs/heads/` and `refs/tags/` (present locally after a `fetch --no-prune`) and the head of `refs/pull/<n>/head` with `--pr <n>`. No local ref is a keeper. It deletes a proven candidate only when no worktree has it checked out. The output drops `branch_deleted` and `branch_only_commits`, and adds `branches` and `lock`.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh`: 218 checks, with new checks for each wait, each lock case, each candidate source, each keeper and non-keeper, and the usage errors of `--pr`.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md`: states the new `stop` wait, the `remove` wait, the lock rule, the candidates, the proof, the output fields and the exit codes.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/resume-and-close.md`: step 2 needs no second `remove`; step 3 gives `--delete-branch --pr <pr.number>` for a merged PR and `--delete-branch` alone when `pr` is `null`, and puts one notice for every branch that stays. The close of a run points at step 3 for its flags.
- `README.md`: the close also deletes the item's branches, and a branch whose commits are not on origin or a PR head stays.
- `docs/design.md`: entry 15.147.
- `CLAUDE.md`: one Build state sentence.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: version 0.1.114.

### Constraints that applied

- Issue 156's rule: no command deletes a commit that exists nowhere else. This change proves more than §15.145 did: a local branch, a stale remote-tracking ref and a local tag are no longer proof, so one candidate cannot prove another and two closes at the same time cannot prove each other's branches.
- No force anywhere: no `--force` on `git worktree remove`, no unlock without the dead-owner proof, no `git branch -D` of an unproven candidate. `stop` signals no process.
- Python 3.9: both tests run on `/usr/bin/python3` (3.9.6).
- The test makes its own repos, worktrees, branches, `$HOME` and `$CREW_RECORD_ROOT`, and starts no real `claude`.
- A rule lives in one file: `resume-and-close.md` points at `launcher.md` for the proof and copies none of it.
- Version bump in both manifests, equal values.

### How this was verified

- `PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh`: 218 of 218 checks passed. The red commits (`efd84ef`, `8e78be4`) failed 28 and 7 of the new checks before each fix.
- `PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-orch.sh`: all checks passed.
- A spec critic read the spec, and a skeptical review read the finished diff on the local head before the first push: 0 blocking, 3 suggestions and 1 nit, all four fixed in the second round (`8e78be4` to `3a6b621`). The project lead read the whole `launcher.py` diff.

### Known gaps

- Only the seeded test has run the new code. No orchestrator has closed an item with it.
- The `stop` and `remove` waits are not proven against a live `claude` that ends after its tab closes.
- A package branch of a run whose PR was rebased and later changed by fix commits cannot be proven, and stays with a notice, as the ticket accepts.
- `CLAUDE.md` was over its 200-line target before this change; this change adds one sentence.

triage.summary: The change makes the close of an orchestrator item run in one pass. `stop` now waits for the claude processes to end after it closes the tab. `remove` waits for an ending session, handles a worktree lock whose owner is dead, and deletes every branch of the item that origin, or the PR head via a new `--pr` flag, can prove holds the commits. The output changes from `branch_deleted` and `branch_only_commits` to `branches` and `lock`. Docs, tests and a version bump come with it.

findings.claim: This test checks the exact git argument lists (ls-remote, rev-list --stdin, branch -D) when it could check the behaviour that results.
findings.evidence: check 'remove --delete-branch reads the keepers with ls-remote origin, proves with rev-list --stdin and no local ref, and deletes with branch -D' \
findings.suggested_fix: Drop this check and rely on the keeper and non-keeper tests, which check the result.
findings.explanation: A different git command with the same result would fail this test. The stale-ref and local-tag tests already check that no local ref counts as a keeper.
